title: Multiplication invariant
statement: For lists $z$ and $S$, write the defaulted pair decomposition of $z$ as $(X,Y)$. The multiplication invariant holds when there are lists $A,B,C$ such that $S$ encodes $(A,(B,C))$, the binary value of $C$ plus the product of the binary values of $A$ and $B$ equals the product of the binary values of $X$ and $Y$, $C$ is the canonical binary representation of its value, and the combined lengths of $A$ and $B$ are at most the combined lengths of $X$ and $Y$.
caveat: The supplied statement omits the definitions and conventions for pair encoding, defaulted projections, binary value, and canonical bit representation.
